Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1225 PM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM THE UPPER 
OHIO VALLEY INTO THE CAROLINAS AND PARTS OF GEORGIA...AND OVER A
PART OF THE NORTHERN PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated occurrences of mainly damaging winds are possible from the
upper Ohio Valley into the Carolinas and parts of Georgia Sunday
afternoon and evening. A more conditional severe risk exists across
parts of North Dakota into far northwest Minnesota late Sunday
night.

...Synopsis...
Weak troughing will bring modest flow and broad ascent across much
of the eastern US. Enhanced westerly flow will overspread the
northern periphery of the western ridge across the Northern Rockies
as a more progressive mid-level low moves across the Canadian
Prairies. 

At the surface, an occluding surface low will shift northeast across
the Ohio Valley into the Northeast, with a trailing cold front
slowly shifting east across the Ohio Valley into the Gulf States. A
cold front will shift across portions of the Northern Rockies into
the northern Plains.

...Upper Ohio Valley into the Southeast...
Broad forcing for ascent within the region of the eastward sagging
cold front will produce widely scattered thunderstorm activity
across much of the region from the Ohio Valley to the Southeast.
Activity will likely be ongoing at the start of the period from the
northern Ohio Valley into the Appalachians. Broken mid-level cloud
cover behind the morning convection should allow for sufficient
heating/destabilization and moderate instability ahead of the cold
front by the afternoon. This in combination with deep layer shear
around 25-35 kts will support isolated strong storms capable of
damaging wind where better heating can occur. 

...Northern Plains...
A conditional severe threat will extend across potions of North
Dakota into northern Minnesota. Within this region, the environment
will be favorable for severe storms, with moderate to strong
instability and strong deep layer shear. However, weak forcing for
ascent and strong capping at the base of the EML during the daytime
heating period may limit development until mid-level cooling and
ascent from the upper wave moves in late. Nonetheless, should a cell
or two develop the environment would support potential for large
hail and damaging wind. It appears most likely that convection
develops along the cold front toward the end of the D2 period, with
potential for large hail and damaging wind.

..Thornton.. 08/01/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0227 PM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER EASTERN NORTH
 DAKOTA...NORTHWEST MINNESOTA...AND A SMALL PART OF NORTHEAST SOUTH
DAKOTA......

...SUMMARY...
Widely scattered to scattered severe storms are expected across
eastern North Dakota, northwest Minnesota, and a small part of
northeast South Dakota Monday. Severe wind gusts and large hail will
be the primary hazards. Isolated damaging winds are possible from
central and eastern South Dakota into western Nebraska, and in
portions of the Mid-Atlantic into southern New England.

...Synopsis...
A progressive wave with unseasonably strong mid-level flow will
eject across the northern Plains into the upper Midwest on
D3/Monday.  At the surface, a low will develop from western SD into
northern MN, with a cold front advancing through the northern Plains
and upper MS Valley. The southern extension of the front will push
into the central High Plains.

...Northern and central Plains into the upper Mississippi Valley...
Convection is expected to be ongoing near the front across portions
of North Dakota into western Minnesota Friday morning as height
falls overspread the region near the cold front. Early day storms
may be elevated, likely posing the best potential for a few
instances of large hail. Behind morning convection, steep low to
mid-level lapse rates and clearing should allow for a swath of
moderate instability to develop across western North Dakota into
northern Minnesota by the afternoon. Thunderstorm activity is
expected to redevelop near the front during this time. Supercell
wind profiles will be in place with potential for large hail and
damaging wind. High LCLs will likely limit the tornado potential.

The air mass further south across South Dakota into southern
central/Minnesota will likely remained capped and free of morning
convection. Stronger heating and moistening in this region may
result in moderate to strong instability. A conditional threat for
supercells will be possible, limited by remaining capping at the
base of the EML through the afternoon. Should storms develop, the
environment would support the potential for isolated occurrences of
severe wind gusts and perhaps some large hail.

...Southern New England into the Mid-Atlantic...
Storms will likely be ongoing at the start of the period across
southern  New England into the Mid-Atlantic, which leads to
uncertainty in the degree of air mass destabilization by afternoon
along and ahead of the front. Where filtered heating can occur, the
presence of a moist air mass will support pockets of moderate
instability by afternoon. Forcing within the right entrance region
of an upper-level jet streak lifting through northern New England
will combine with the front to yield an increase in storms through
the afternoon within a kinematic environment featuring 30-35 kt of
deep-layer shear. As such, a few strong to severe storms appear
possible, with the primary hazard being damaging wind gusts.

..Thornton.. 08/01/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0317 AM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 041200Z - 091200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Tuesday...

A broader-scale trough is forecast over central Canada into the
north-central U.S. with a series of subtle disturbances moving
through the base of that feature. At the surface, a front is
expected to move through the upper Great Lakes with the western
extension of the boundary settling slowly south through the central
High Plains. A severe weather threat may materialize from the mid MO
Valley into the central High Plains along the front and in the
post-frontal upslope, where an overlap of moderate instability and
stronger vertical shear is expected to reside.

Elsewhere, a more widespread area of moderate instability developing
across southern AZ could support a locally greater risk of severe
storms. 

The extent of the severe weather threat in both areas is currently
too uncertain to delineate an area. 
 

...Day 5/Wednesday...

The broad, cyclonic flow regime will continue over the north-central
CONUS with a belt of slightly enhanced mid-level winds extending
from the northern Rockies through the northern and central Plains
into the Great Lakes. At the surface, the previously mentioned front
will continue through the Great Lakes with the boundary extending
southwest through the mid MS Valley into the central or southern
High Plains. Similar to Day 4/Tuesday, some severe weather appears
possible along the boundary over the lower MO into mid MS Valleys,
as well as within the post-frontal upslope across the central High
Plains. 

The subtle nature of the forcing for ascent leads to uncertainty in
severe storm coverage, so no area will be included. 


...Days 6-8/Thursday through Saturday...

The 00Z ensemble means are in reasonably good agreement in depicting
the continuation of an upper high over the southwestern U.S. with
lower-amplitude troughing over the Great Lakes into the Northeast.
At the surface, there is considerable model spread in the location
of relevant boundaries that might focus severe storms. That being
said, much of the available AI guidance suggests an increasing
severe weather threat in the Mid-Atlantic during this time frame. 

Model trends will continue to be monitored for the possible
inclusion of an area in subsequent outlooks.

..Mead.. 08/01/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0744 PM CDT Sat Aug 01 2026

Valid 020100Z - 021200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS EVENING
ACROSS PARTS OF THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS AND PARTS OF THE
SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS/ROCKIES...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms posing a risk for generally brief, weak tornadoes
across the southwestern Ohio vicinity probably will begin to
diminish within the next hour or two.  Otherwise, locally strong to
severe gusts remain possible this evening in continuing thunderstorm
development across parts of the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys, and
parts of the southern Rockies into adjacent southern Great Plains.

...01Z Update...

...Ohio/Tennessee Valleys...
Focused low-level convergence and weak to modest clockwise-curved
low-level hodographs, near a surface low now centered to the
northwest of the Greater Cincinnati area, have contributed to
transient supercell structures within developing convection
downstream of an elongating mid-level low across the lower
Ohio/middle Mississippi Valley vicinity.  Potential for brief/weak
tornadoes has probably been boosted by near-surface buoyancy
associated with a boundary layer characterized by high relative
humidity and surface dew points in the lower 70s, along at least a
narrow pre-frontal corridor near the southern Ohio/Indiana state
border area into north central Kentucky.  However, with the loss of
daytime heating, near-surface stabilization probably will diminish
this threat by 02-03Z.

Otherwise, some intensification of pre-frontal thunderstorm
development still appears possible this evening, southward across
parts of middle and eastern Tennessee into northern Alabama. 
Although lower/mid-tropospheric lapse rates are rather modest to
weak, seasonably high moisture content is supporting sizable CAPE. 
Aided by 20-30 kt deep-layer southwesterly mean flow overspreading
this environment, heavy precipitation loading and downward momentum
transfer could still contribute to potential for localized damaging
surface gusts.

...Southern Rockies and adjacent southern Great Plains...
Convection developing southward ahead of a weak perturbation within
light northerly flow, into a very warm and deeply mixed boundary
layer with 40-50 F surface temperature/dew point spreads, may
continue to pose a risk for strong to locally severe wind gusts into
mid/late evening across parts of southern New Mexico and adjacent
portions of western/southwestern Texas and southeastern Arizona.

..Kerr.. 08/02/2026

$$
